chunks: Hadith 4569 — Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Saʿdān ibn Muslim, from Abū Baṣīr, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them:

Concerning a man who married off his bondwoman to a free man for four hundred dirhams, and he paid two hundred dirhams in advance for him, then delayed two hundred dirhams from him. Her husband then consummated the marriage with her. After that, her master sold her to another man. Upon whom are the two hundred dirhams that were deferred?

So he said: If he had not paid her the remainder of the mahr before he sold her, then nothing is due from him to her or to anyone else. And when the master sells her, she has become separated from the free husband, if he knew this matter.

key_terms.الْمَهْرِ: the dowry owed in the marriage contract
key_terms.الْمُؤَخَّرَتَانِ: the two hundred dirhams whose payment was deferred
key_terms.حُرٍّ: a free man, as opposed to a slave
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: a monetary unit used here for the mahr amount
key_terms.مَمْلُوكَةً: a female bondwoman owned by a master

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a deferred mahr when a bondwoman is sold after being married to a free man?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning a bondwoman married to a free man with a deferred mahr, then sold by her master after consummation. It states that if the deferred portion was not paid before the sale, nothing remains due, and the sale separates her from the free husband if he knew this ruling.
